Starship V3 is designed to carry around 100 tonnes to orbit per launch

For comparison, SpaceX put 2,213 tonnes into orbit in all of 2025

That's more than 20 TIMES SpaceX's entire 2025 orbital payload, from just ONE launch site

And this is before adding Starship launch sites in Florida and elsewhere

SpaceX is building toward an entirely different scale of access to space

posts.text:
Connect your ChatGPT and Claude subscriptions to Grok @bot with the prompt below (@elonmusk approved):

Connect my Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions so all of my bots can use them.

1. On your computer, install the Claude Code CLI and the OpenAI Codex CLI (upgrade Node if needed). Start each subscription login (Claude: `claude setup-token`; Codex: `codex login --device-auth`) and send me the sign-in links and codes. I'll sign in and paste back anything you need. Store the Claude token privately and load it automatically.

2. Set the defaults to these models: Claude Opus 5.5 for Claude Code and 6.1 Sol for Codex. Test each one with a quick prompt and tell me which models answered.

3. Add these MODEL ROUTING RULES to every one of my bots' system prompts, including yours. Keep everything else in each prompt exactly as it is:
   - Writing (drafts, emails, posts, replies, copy, briefs): write the final text with Claude through the CLI, then review it against the bot's voice rules.
   - Coding, scripts, data processing, and terminal work: use Codex.
   - Browser and desktop tasks: keep using your normal computer tools.
   - If either CLI fails, do the task yourself and say so.

4. Save the same rule to my shared memory so any bot I create later follows it too.

5. When you're done, tell me which bots you updated and confirm both tests passed.

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
$SPCX isn't just building compute faster than every other neocloud

It has something none of them have: OPTIONALITY on every GPU it deploys

Every GW SpaceX brings online has two paths to revenue:

1. use it for Grok / xAI and capture the frontier model economics themselves, which generates more revenue than renting it out (Semianalysis estimates around $100B/GW)

2. rent it out to everyone else, at a premium

The reason SpaceX can rent out their compute at a premium is twofold:

1. Speed. SpaceX builds faster than anyone on earth, so they can get compute into customers' hands faster than any competitor. AI labs that need compute NOW pay up for that

2. The backstop. SpaceX can sign short-term contracts at higher prices because if a customer backs out, that compute simply goes to their own AI models. No empty racks, no panic

CoreWeave and Nebius can't take that risk, so they lock in most long-term deals at lower rents and fund the buildout with debt

Which brings us to funding, which is where the gap between these companies gets even wider

SpaceX doesn't have to fund the buildout (or the interest costs) from compute revenue alone. Starlink and launch cash flows can carry part of it. CoreWeave is paying 15% on unsecured bonds right now while SpaceX has diversified revenue streams across the whole company (and the best capital raiser alive running it)

And the part almost nobody is pricing in: as compute moves to space in the next few years, SpaceX owns the cheapest path to win there too. The rockets that bring the compute up AND the connectivity that beams it back down

That's why the chart above looks the way it does. Bloomberg Intelligence models SpaceX's AI ROIC going from negative 4% in 2026 to ~25% by 2030, above AWS and Google Cloud, while the pure neoclouds stay stuck in single digits

No one is better positioned to dominate the compute business in the coming years than SpaceX

This is why I still believe SpaceX is undervalued and why I've made it a core holding in my Milk Road PRO portfolio. You can see my entire real-time portfolio here: https://link.milkroad.com/t5837z

quote.author: KyleReidhead
quote.name: Kyle Reidhead | Milk Road
quote.text:
Is SpaceX competition hurting the valuation / credit risk of Neoclouds?

$CRWV and $NBIS down 10%+ today, while $SPCX down just 2% (and UP on the month)

The obvious trigger is credit risk, with CoreWeave's unsecured bonds yielding 15%

But in the last week, Elon also confirmed that SpaceX will reach 2GW by November and potentially 2.6 GW by EOY. That's .6GW ahead of schedule and quickly becoming much bigger than Coreweave and Nebius

Almost no one building compute is doing it ahead of schedule, but SpaceX is proving to be superior here on speed and is expecting close to 10GW by 2027 (And significantly more in years ahead, especially as we move to compute in Space)

At the same time, Elon also mentioned earlier this week about the difficulty in executing this build out (said even SpaceX engineers are finding it hard) but also in the ability for companies to raise capital... the issue Coreweave is having now.

But we know SpaceX and Elon has no issues in raising capital (and generating revenue from other sources too). Raising capital is what Elon excels at over anyone

So I wonder if the market is starting to see that SpaceX is becoming a very big competitor to these neoclouds, taking demand sure... though I think there is plenty of demand to go around.. but more so taking resources and capital that other neoclouds need to scale

SpaceX also has optionality to either rent out the compute or use it for xAI / Grok, which lowers risk even further to fund their compute buildout. It's also why SpaceX can charge a premium on their compute vs the other neoclouds, lowering risk even further

I'm not saying SpaceX is the full reason for Coreweaves issues, but you gotta think this evolving competitive landscape of Elon entering the ring has to have something to do with it

Even with this said, I'm still bullish on neoclouds as I think the demand remains endless, but I think SpaceX becomes the dominate neocloud by next year

quote.author: SawyerMerritt
quote.name: Sawyer Merritt
quote.text:
SpaceX has just introduced Grok Voice 3.0

"It's the world’s most intelligent speech-to-speech model. It sets a new record for resolving customer support calls, has class-leading latency at under one second, and costs less than other frontier models. It's also cheaper to run than comparable models. Artificial Analysis measures what each model costs to complete a task in its Big Bench Audio run, and Grok Voice 3.0 comes in under both GPT-Live-1 (Astra, Medium) and GPT-Realtime-2.1.

Grok Voice 3.0 handles millions of conversations a day in Tesla vehicles. Drivers can use Connectors for simple requests like checking their calendar or answering an email, and Grok Bot for bigger tasks like ordering a coffee or booking dinner—all completely hands-free (see it on X). Grok Voice 3.0 also powers Grok Bot’s voice mode."

More info: https://x.ai/news/grok-voice-3
